elements.contractorWeeksPerYear: The ONLY place unpaid vacation, holidays, sick days, and bench time are modeled. Reducing weeks lowers gross revenue directly.
elements.contractorOverheadPercent: Simple mode. Covers only costs NOT captured by fewer billable weeks: employer-share payroll taxes, health insurance, lost retirement match, business expenses. Documented default range 20-30%. Must never include vacation or unpaid time - that would double-count against Weeks/Year.
elements.extraPayrollTaxPercent: The extra tax burden versus an employee. US default 7.65% (the employer half of FICA). A documented default, not a universal figure: income thresholds (Social Security wage base) and the deductibility of the employer-equivalent portion shift the exact burden.
elements.lostPensionMatchPercent: Employer retirement match the contractor no longer receives. Typical US 401(k) match 3-6% of salary; default 4%.
elements.riskPremiumPercent: Optional buffer for income volatility, dry spells, and client concentration. Default 0; the freelance-risk-calculator prices this explicitly.
elements.healthInsuranceDeltaAnnual: The annual difference between self-funded coverage and the employee's subsidized plan, not the full premium. Default $8,000 (US individual marketplace vs typical employer subsidy).
elements.adminSoftwareInsuranceAnnual: Accounting, invoicing software, liability insurance, legal. Default $3,000.

constraints: Unpaid time off must affect the result through contractorWeeksPerYear only, never through overhead.
Increasing contractorHourlyRate must never decrease contractorNetEquivalent.
In simple mode, contractorNetEquivalent must equal contractorGross * (1 - overhead/100) exactly - overhead is applied once.

sources.name: IRS Self-Employment Tax (15.3% total; 7.65% is the employer half)
